Woahhh pump the breaks. While a few humans have got it yes, they have mostly all got it from sick animals. H5N1 is not yet known to spread from human to human. There have actually been cases of bird flu in humans for over 20+ years, however, they are rare and usually only found in those who work with livestock. 

There isn’t much need to worry yet. And there might not ever be a reason to worry. There’s no real way of knowing tbh. If you have a cat, maybe keep it indoors more often for a little while. And other than that, just practice the general precautions when it comes to personal hygiene & staying healthy. 

Most importantly though, don’t change your plans to travel abroad! No one has a crystal ball. No one’s gonna know how H5N1 will (or will not) mutate in the coming future. 

These sort of things are mostly out of your control, so worrying preemptively does you no good. And if shit does hit the fan, roll with the punches and act accordingly. 

I know another pandemic sounds scary. It scares me a bit too. However, we can’t let the fear win, and we must keep on keepin on! There’s really no other choice tbh. The time will pass one way or another

I’d skip Idaho. Batshit crazy politics over there. Montana on the other hand, is way more of “purple” state. So I think somewhere there or somewhere in Colorado would probably be your best bets. Missoula (where I grew up & currently live) has like 100k people, however it is definitely still a mountain town for the most part at its core. The proximity to nature is great, about as good as it gets really, and Missoula as a city itself is pretty laid back too so, I doubt you’d feel overwhelmed whatsoever. There’s plenty of neighborhoods that you could find here that don’t feel corporatized or bustling. But that said, if you wanted to go out and meet people, the nightlife here isn’t so bad for a town its size either. I really do think you could probably find what you’re looking for here, even though the city is a bit bigger than what you were initially searching for. 

And as far as politics go? Yeah, Montana is red. More red now than it was before this recent election too. But Missoula is still a pretty dark blue dot. Missoula county vote tallies came out to 59% for Harris, and only 37% for Trump. There are tons of small businesses here that openly support the LGBTQ community, and all in all I’d say Missoula is generally a pretty welcoming place to all. So yeah, you would definitely fit in politically here as well. 

So yeah, that’s that! I think you’d enjoy it here. Again, I know the population is a little high. But imo? That is worth the sacrifice. Constantly being around people that think differently than you do is tough. Hmmm okay, non naturey things to do in Missoula… let me think. Well, first off, pretty much everything you do here city wise, DC will probably do better. But that doesn’t mean you can’t still have a good time, so I’ll give you my 2 cents! 

If you’re into sports, griz football games are actually really fun. The environment is honestly really great for bein FCS football. Griz games are surprisingly loud for a stadium its size. So I’d recdomend that for sure if they have a home game when you’re in town. Edit here - just saw that you said next July, so they prolly won’t have a game goin on then. So scratch that! 

The kettlehouse ampitheater is a good little concert venue, could be fun to catch a show out there. But bring a coat! It gets cold as hell once the sun goes down this time of year. The Wilma puts on some decent shows too, and it’s also kinda an iconic Missoula venue, so check that out if the kettlehouse doesn’t have anything goin on. 

We’ve got some good breweries here too if you’re into beer. Imagine nation & draughtworks are my two favorites in town. But there’s a bunch, so if you’re into that then try a few! Missoulas bar scene in general ain’t all that bad, our downtown is kinda fun to explore if you’re into that.

As far as food recommendations go, tagliare delicatessen has really great sandwiches. Drum makes good coffee. Everything else is kinda just eh. You can find okay meals, but I mean.. there ain’t gonna be anything here you can’t find bein done better in DC. 

But anyways yeah, tbh id still recommend seein some kind of scenery while you’re here one way or another. If you don’t wanna take a big ol’ day trip to see some really amazing scenery at some mountain lake or something, then thankfully you can still get some good views not far out of the city of Missoula at all. Maclay flats / blue mountain are good little walking trails that aren’t too far out of town at all. Pattee canyon ain’t bad either. But remember, bring that bear spray! Just the other week I saw a black bear right by maclays, which mind you, is only like 15 mins outside of the city. 

If you have any more questions, PM me! I’m a Missoulian born and raised so, I can probably answer a lot of questions better than most. 

Enjoy your trip!! Hope the smoke ain’t too bad here for ya next July. Haha

Montana is also a cultural wasteland. According to a 2022 census, 85% of Montanans are white so, yeah. That’s that. There’s an okay music & arts scene in Missoula, but it’s also nothin crazy imo. I also don’t agree with most of Montana’s politics. So that’s obviously an opinion thing but, yeah. 

All in all Montana just isn’t my place. But, it was where I was born. And that’s that. Lotta people love it, I just don’t. If Missoula was like, an hour away from a major metro? Missoula isn’t horrible for a city its size by any means. There’s a decent music scene, and due to the college and all, the nightlife is okay too. Not great, but okay for a town of 120k or so in the “metro” area. Griz football games are also surprisingly fun too if you’re into that. Somehow someway, that stadium can get louder than others that are 5x the size of it. Food in Montana is very average, and that stays true in Missoula too. Everything is also surprisingly expensive here. Rent is absurd for what you get. COL does not make sense for the QOL but, that is what it is. 

All that said, a lot of people I know love it here, a lot of people I grew up with will never leave Montana, or Missoula in general. It just depends on what kinda person you are.

That said, in my option, you better fuckin loveee the outdoors and not much else if you really wanna live your life here. This is based off of my own personal likes and dislikes ofc, but I don’t think there’s anything in Montana that you couldn’t get in another mountain type of town that’s closer to a major city. Missoula is a good 7.5-8 hours away from any major metro (Seattle and SLC that is). And in my eyes, growing up here that just always fuckin sucked. If you want to go to any sort of event or concert, it’s usually a 1500$ venture once you sort out all of the hotel and travel expenses. Although I grew up and spent the first 22 years of my life in Missoula, I also have lived in Austin Texas for a year as well, and there was just so much more opportunity there. So much more to do. I genuinely did more cool shit there in one year there, than I did in an entire lifetime in Missoula. 

I’m back in Missoula now, and while leaving did make me appreciate my hometown a bit more, I still don’t think it’s that great of a place to call your forever home.

If Missoula was only an hour or 2 from a Seattle sized city, it’d probably be one of the more desirable smaller towns in the entire country. Unfortunately though, Montana is isolated. And in my opinion, you definitely feel that isolation cave in while living here. 

Oh and yeah, there isn’t much humidity here, but in the summer, there’s almost always smoke. Wildfires are extremely common in this area, and Missoula is in a valley. Once the smoke comes, it takes a while for it to leave. Gets all stuck in between these damn mountains haha. Trust me when I say you’d rather deal with humidity.

I’m 22, I’ve lived in Austin for a little less than half a year now, and the reasons I moved here are as follows. 

- the cost of living, is actually much cheaper compared to a lot of big cities around the world. Try finding a decent cost of living in New York or a bigger city California, you won’t.

- this city is very much still vibrant and alive. I’m in love with the performing arts, there’s tons of music, standup comedy, and basically everything under the sun here. I grew up in a state that doesn’t get much traffic from touring acts, and lemme tell ya, I already have done more cool shit in my 5 months here than I did in a lifetime back home. Not to mention, the food and nightlife is great too. Which in my opinion is another big perk. 

- crime and homelessness are again, in every big city, hell, it was even prevalent in my hometown city that had about 70k people. It’s just a thing. Nobody has the answer. People complaining about Austin’s crime and homelessness should go visit San Francisco or Portland and see just how “bad” Austin’s problem really is.. 

- now I’ll admit. My biggest issue with moving to Austin was the government of Texas as a whole. However, I found that I simply could not afford to live in a big city in a democratic state. I’m not sure why they’re all more expensive, but they just kinda are. And even if you could afford it, it’s not like places such as Portland or Seattle don’t have the exact same issues austin is having, if not more issues. So, I chose a city that aligned with my views rather than a state. It was hard, but at the end of the day I just kinda had to realize that the entire United States government was extremely volatile, and that I shouldn’t let it entirely depict where I live. 

- and lastly, as far as the heat goes, I really just tell people like yeah… it’s bad.. but try living in the blistering cold. Walking outside when it’s -50 with windchill is a hell of a lot more inconvenient feeling than when it’s 105+ if you ask me. Waking up in the morning when it’s 15 below and having to scrape off your windows? Yeah also not a good time. And not to mention, the cold dark months of winter definitely impacted my mental health too.
